items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: So I thought, I'm going to do that one day, and I did.

ctx.x: Where did you run into Lovey Austin?

I ran into Lovey Austin when I was about 8 or 9 or 10 years old. I must have been pretty small because my brother-in-law used to throw me on his shoulder if I went to sleep in the theatre, and bring me home like that. He took me up there to see her, what she was doing. She had her legs crossed, with a cigarette in her mouth, playing and writing music for the next act. When the next act came on, the music was ready. She'd pass it out to the musicians who were going to play it. So I thought, I'm going to do that…
Why did you want to do it?
